messages:
Jamal R: Hey everyone, first day — I got the company ThinkPad (T14) with Ubuntu 22.04 preinstalled. Trying to run the Device Trust / fleet enrollment agent but it fails with 'device-trust: no TPM detected' and the MDM agent exits. Disk is LUKS-encrypted out of the box. Who should I ping for help getting this enrolled so I can access repos? :wave:
it-support: Welcome Jamal! Can you paste the exact error and the machine serial? Also run these and paste output: `sudo cryptsetup luksDump /dev/nvme0n1p3` and `ls /sys/class/tpm` — that'll tell us if kernel sees a TPM device.
Jamal R: Serial: RDXT1234567. Error: `error: device-trust: failed to get tpm handle: no device`
Jamal R: Output of `ls /sys/class/tpm`: (empty)
it-support: ok — empty list means kernel isn't exposing the TPM. Two common causes: BIOS TPM disabled or firmware set to 'discrete' vs 'firmware' and not exposed. Also sometimes Secure Boot interplay.
Eli: Hi Jamal — tagging infra. If BIOS has 'TPM 2.0' and it's enabled, we should see something. If the vendor image pre-provisioned LUKS keys, toggling TPM can be risky. Don't clear the TPM. If you're comfortable, we can remote and try a non-invasive check: `dmesg | grep -i tpm` and `sudo modprobe tpm_tis` to see if module loads. I can do a quick remote session and run enrollment shim that works around older firmware quirks.
Marie (security): Quick security note: do not clear or reset the TPM without escrow'ing your disk recovery key. If there's a preprovisioned LUKS key linked to TPM, changing TPM state can lock the device. Create a recovery key and escrow it before we attempt toggles. Use our key-escrow tool: `https://key-escrow.redwood/upload` — file should be encrypted with our public key.
Anna (eng): I can remote in around 15:00 PT today to help with the enrollment. We usually run the fleet enroll script with sudo for a few commands and then revert any temp changes. Jamal, can you drop a calendar invite for 15:00 PT? I'll be on the session and bring the enrollment logs tool. :calendar:
Jamal R: Thanks — copying outputs here from `sudo cryptsetup luksDump /dev/nvme0n1p3`:
  LUKS header information
  Version:        2
  Cipher name:    aes
  Cipher mode:    xts-plain64
  Payload offset: 4096
  MK bits:        256
  Keyslots:       1
Jamal R: I haven't created a recovery key yet. I'll do that and escrow it now. Also ok for 15:00 PT.
it-support: To create a new key (if you have a passphrase currently): `sudo cryptsetup luksAddKey /dev/nvme0n1p3` — follow prompts, then upload to key escrow. If the current key is vendor-set and you can't add, stop and we'll escalate.
Eli: If `modprobe tpm_tis` yields nothing, try `sudo apt install --reinstall --yes fwupd` then `sudo fwupdmgr get-devices` — some Lenovo firmwares need firmwared updates to expose TPM properly. We'll only request that if you consent.
Marie (security): Confirmed — don't advise any TPM clearing. We'll only do read-only checks until escrowed.
Anna (eng): I'll take the call and run the enrollment steps. Plan: 1) confirm escrow, 2) attempt modprobe and dmesg checks, 3) run enrollment shim (time-limited sudo), 4) re-check LUKS header and confirm keys still valid.
Jamal R: Sounds good — thanks all. Sending invite to anna@redwood.com and uploading the escrow now. Appreciate the quick help! :lock:
